title: Persistent Systems says employee immigration data was purportedly exfiltrated from a US law firm it uses
date_note: IANS (23 Nov) says Persistent made the disclosure on Monday, 23 November, in a stock exchange filing; the page gives no date for the incident at the law firm. The filing itself was not read.
org: Persistent Systems (third-party US law firm, not named)
geo_basis: country: IANS says the law firm is US-based and does not name its city
sector: Professional and legal services (third party of an IT services company)
summary: Persistent Systems said in a stock exchange filing on Monday that a US-based law firm handling its immigration matters may have suffered a cybersecurity incident, IANS reports. Persistent said certain employee immigration data and supporting documentation was purportedly exfiltrated from that law firm. The company said the incident concerns the external firm, not its own systems, which it says are secure, and that claims its critical information was stolen are unverified.
plain: Indian IT company Persistent Systems says a US law firm that handles its staff immigration matters may have been hacked, and that some employee immigration papers were purportedly taken. It says its own systems are secure.
exec: Persistent Systems says employee immigration data was purportedly taken from a US law firm it uses, while its own systems are secure.

validation.note: Only the IANS article, which quotes Persistent's stock exchange filing, was read. Moneycontrol's report would not load for the reader; the filing was not on Persistent's investor announcements page when checked.

review.note: Compared title, summary, date and hedges against the IANS article quoting the filing; single_source correct
